candidate.mechanism: Ownership of medium intraday-to-swing volatility reversion: participants providing liquidity at slower horizons (swing mean-reverters) act as payers over hours-to-days, enabling larger moves relative to cost
candidate.payer: slower-horizon liquidity providers and mean-reversion demand
candidate.entry_event: sustained high intraday volatility spike with order-flow exhaustion signals on 15–60m aggregation (large returns with shrinking aggressive flow share)
candidate.regime_owner: active in episodic volatility-spike regimes with evidence of post-spike mean-reversion; inactive in sustained trending volatility regimes
candidate.invalidation: If volatility spikes no longer mean-revert within the extended horizon (structural regime shift to trending spikes), mechanism invalidated
candidate.exit_logic: exit when volatility and aggressive-flow exhaustion reverse to normal regime or when larger-timeframe trend resumes; horizon governed by regime reversion, not fixed thresholds
candidate.time_stop_rationale: hours-to-days horizon aligns with mean-reversion timescale of volatility spikes and allows move size to dominate round-trip costs
candidate.turnover_cost_budget: longer horizon targets larger expected moves (>=2x cost) by waiting for swing-scale reversion funded by slower liquidity
candidate.falsification: Prospective kill if realized reversion magnitude within the extended horizon fails to exceed expected move-cost multiple on >55% of triggers across a 90-day out-of-sample period
candidate.why_distinct: Alters only the native holding horizon compared to baseline, shifting to multi-hour/swing context — single-axis repair

supports.limitation: Supports regime-dependent intraday momentum/reversal, not this exact BingX executable rule.
Supports jump/order-flow mechanism; current BingX transferability and swing-horizon economics require development evidence.

features.name: volatility_spike_state
features.mechanism: episodic large realized moves create a candidate reversion state when shock pressure is temporary
features.observable: closed OHLCV returns and realized range/volatility on 15–60m aggregation
features.direction: fade the spike only when exhaustion and regime conditions agree
features.invalidation: continued expansion with trend persistence contradicts mean-reversion ownership

features.name: aggressive_flow_exhaustion
features.mechanism: shrinking aggressive participation after a spike indicates marginal taker pressure is exhausting
features.direction: confirm reversion only when aggressive flow contracts after the spike
features.invalidation: persistent or increasing aggressive flow indicates informed continuation rather than exhaustion

features.name: volume_context
features.mechanism: volume distinguishes a material volatility event from ordinary range noise and provides context for exhaustion
features.observable: closed-bar volume and its local history
features.direction: use volume as event context, not as an outcome filter
features.invalidation: no material event participation or inconsistent volume context removes the causal setup
